archetypes.name: bash-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan hinges on exact bash-vs-Python parity across finalize, cleanup, and force-push contracts.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the proposed Python changes against the referenced bash scripts and verify that the plan targets the right branch conditions, status tokens, ordering, and failure behavior. Look for places where the plan assumes parity helpers exist, names the wrong bash authority, or omits an observable bash branch that would make parity tests incomplete. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: state-plumbing
archetypes.rationale: The plan spans finalize, ship, run_logs, and ci_monitor state transitions where partial propagation can silently drift.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the proposed status and state fields across finalize.py, run_logs.py, ship.py, and ci_monitor.py. Check whether the plan accounts for every caller, persisted state value, recovery flag, and skip path needed to prevent stale ctx, lost pending-rebase state, or report/write execution after failed recovery. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-gate
archetypes.rationale: The plan’s success depends on real parity coverage and fail-closed behavior rather than smoke or all-skip tests.
archetypes.prompt_body: Evaluate whether the proposed unit and bash-parity test plan would actually catch the listed divergences and fail closed when bash is available. Look for missing fixtures, impossible stubbing assumptions, untested status fields, Makefile/doc target drift, or claims that conflict with existing pytest skip mechanics. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
